- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to cap the peak; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and smooth the slope downward.
- If model forecast mean is significantly above true outcome mean (e.g., >5% over 30d), apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment volatility (more if sentiment is erratic).
- When sentiment is positive but model shows strong downward trend, it may be overreacting to short-term noise; add a small upward bias (e.g., +1–2% to mean) to preserve upside potential.
- Model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements; increase forecast weights on recent history (e.g., 30% more weight on last 7 days) if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment is stable or neutral, model tends to overfit to recent noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce false peaks and troughs.
